sources.title: North San José Area Development Policy

office.label: Downtown San Jose
office.oneLineDistinction: Civic, technology and university activity in the urban core
office.shortDescription: Downtown San Jose concentrates civic institutions, offices, San José State University, entertainment and convention uses in the city’s most walkable commercial core. Mid- and high-rise buildings distinguish it from North San Jose’s spread-out employment campuses and the lower-rise commercial corridors serving surrounding neighborhoods.
worthKnowing: Street activity and building stock vary across downtown subareas.

office.label: North San Jose
office.oneLineDistinction: Large technology campuses and R&D employment north of I-880
office.shortDescription: North San Jose is one of the city’s largest job centers, with corporate campuses, R&D buildings, office and industrial uses between I-880 and State Route 237. Its broad blocks and campus formats differ sharply from Downtown’s urban grid. Santa Clara, Milpitas and Sunnyvale properties remain outside this City geography.
worthKnowing: Technical capability and municipality must be verified for each address.

retail.label: Santana Row / West San Jose
retail.oneLineDistinction: Destination shopping, dining and services in a planned district
retail.shortDescription: Santana Row and its West San Jose surroundings create a destination-oriented retail setting with restaurants, shops, hotels, offices and residential activity in a planned, walkable format. It differs from Downtown’s civic and entertainment mix and Willow Glen’s smaller neighborhood storefront corridor.
worthKnowing: The district edge approaches Santa Clara; verify municipal ownership.

retail.label: Willow Glen / Lincoln Avenue
retail.oneLineDistinction: Neighborhood storefronts and dining along Lincoln Avenue
retail.shortDescription: Lincoln Avenue forms Willow Glen’s recognizable neighborhood commercial spine, with smaller shops, restaurants and services in a low-rise main-street setting. The format is more local and storefront-oriented than Santana Row’s destination retail or Downtown’s larger civic and entertainment context.
worthKnowing: Customer patterns and frontage vary beyond the core avenue blocks.

industrial.label: Edenvale
industrial.oneLineDistinction: Southern employment land for manufacturing, warehouse and R&D
industrial.shortDescription: Edenvale is a City-recognized employment area in south San Jose with industrial, warehouse, manufacturing and R&D-oriented land. Low-rise operating buildings and larger employment parcels distinguish it from North San Jose’s corporate-campus mix and Downtown’s office core.
worthKnowing: Old and New Edenvale are related components, not interchangeable addresses.

industrial.label: Monterey Corridor
industrial.oneLineDistinction: Linear warehouse and service-industrial land along Monterey Road
industrial.shortDescription: The Monterey Corridor is a long south San Jose employment spine with warehouse, light-industrial, automotive and service-commercial uses along Monterey Road. Its linear frontage and varied parcel formats differ from Edenvale’s broader employment districts and North San Jose’s campus-oriented technology landscape.
worthKnowing: Exact zoning and operating suitability change along the corridor.
